---
title: "Course overview"
subtitle: "Topological data analysis, from first questions to working code"
---

This course is written to be read in order, but each module stands on its own.
Use the menu on the left to jump around; sections open when you click them.

## How the course is organised

1. **[Is TDA applicable?](01-applicability/index.qmd)** Where topological methods have earned their place in research and industry, and where they haven't.
2. **[Potential datasets](02-datasets.qmd)** Point clouds, images, time series and networks to practise on.
3. **[What TDA extracts](03-intuition.qmd)** An intuitive picture of connected components, loops and voids, before any algebra.
4. **[The maths](04-maths/index.qmd)** Algebraic topology, persistent homology, stability, and turning diagrams into features.
5. **[Notebooks](05-notebooks/index.qmd)** Python notebooks that put each idea into practice.

## What you need

Comfort with linear algebra and some Python. The algebraic topology is introduced from scratch.

::: {.callout-note}
## Each lesson includes
A short video, written notes, and a link to the code on GitHub.
:::
